bugs.what: Defeating an enemy via 'parley' (stand-down) does not clear a locked passage guarded by that enemy — a separate grace/will/might check is still required, and this isn't clearly telegraphed the first time it happens (Barrow Crypt wight).

Travel-to-known-place menus paginate in inconsistent groupings (sometimes by region, sometimes by recency) and require several 'more places' clicks to reach a specific far-away location, even though the destination is already known.
bugs.where: travel to a known place menu, throughout

bugs.what: The 'press him (+4 will, 2 turns)' menu option appears occasionally with no explanation of what it does or costs beyond the label; never safe to try blind.
bugs.where: various NPC dialogues, e.g. Old Watchtower, Wardmoor

confusions: First encounter with a 'stood down' enemy still blocking a locked exit was unclear — expected parley/defeat to be equivalent to clearing the path.

It wasn't obvious early on that 'weigh what this grief asks' (free) exists at every major grief-site and previews every resolution path with its costs — I discovered this by accident partway through and it would have saved trial-and-error if flagged more prominently on first arrival.
suggestions: Surface 'weigh what this grief asks' explicitly in the first-visit flavor text for any grief-site, so players know to check it before committing.
When a hostile 'stands down' via parley/buy-off, state directly whether the blocked passage is now open or still needs a separate check.
Add a jump-to-region option or search in the travel menu instead of purely paginated lists once 80+ locations are known.

A small on-screen turn-budget/pace indicator (e.g., 'Act II typically runs 40-70 turns/hold') would help long-run pacing decisions — the status text mentions this but only if the player thinks to check it.
